ios-overlays|Popovers.summary: A Plenix popover on iOS is the system popover, kept native in behavior (the arrow pointing at its source, an outside tap to close, one at a time, a sheet at compact widths, VoiceOver and keyboard) and styled with the Plenix tokens: the overlay surface with the menu border and shadow, DM Sans text and Plenix controls inside, and a popover sized to its content. SwiftUI sets only the background; the 8-point surface radius and border need a UIKit UIPopoverBackgroundView. Apple’s default is a Liquid Glass panel with a 38-point radius.

variants.name: Arrow top
variants.use: The default for a control near the top of the screen; the popover opens below it.

variants.name: Arrow bottom
variants.use: A control near the bottom, such as a toolbar item; the popover opens above it.

variants.name: Arrow leading
variants.use: A control on the leading side, such as a sidebar row; the popover opens toward the content.

variants.name: Arrow trailing
variants.use: A control on the trailing side, such as an inspector button.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.about: The surface that holds a small amount of content, sized to fit it.

anatomy.name: Arrow
anatomy.about: Points at the control that opened the popover, in the surface color.

anatomy.name: Content
anatomy.about: A few related controls or facts in Plenix text roles; no warnings.

swiftui: /// The Plenix popover on iOS: the system popover with the Plenix background and content.
uikit: /// The Plenix popover background: the Plenix radius, border and surface around the system popover.
override class func arrowBase() -> CGFloat { 2 * Plenix.Space.spaceInsetLg }
override class func arrowHeight() -> CGFloat { Plenix.Space.spaceInsetSm }
override var arrowOffset: CGFloat { get { offset } set { offset = newValue; setNeedsLayout() } }
override var arrowDirection: UIPopoverArrowDirection { get { direction } set { direction = newValue; setNeedsLayout() } }
private var offset: CGFloat = 0, direction: UIPopoverArrowDirection = .up
addSubview(box)   // layoutSubviews places box and draws the arrow toward the source
